#Alert Levels
Alert levels represent the danger that is currently directed towards the station. There are 7 alert levels you should look out for.
[color=#00a933]Code Green[/color]: Standard alert at the start of the shift, no danger.
[color=#2a6099]Code Blue[/color]: A danger has been shown to be present on the station
[color=#ff0000]Code Red[/color]: There is active danger towards the station crew.
[color=#ec9ba4]Code Gamma[/color]: There is a threat of total station destruction.
[color=#8d281e]Code Delta[/color]: The onboard nuclear device has been armed, station destruction is imminent.
[color=#8913ff]Code Epsilon[/color]: Extreme circumstances have forced Central Command to take direct control of the station.
[color=#acb20c]Code Yellow[/color]: There is an atmospheric or structural threat to the station.
[color=#ff8119]Code Orange[/color]: The station has taken critical structural damage, and is unlikely to recover.
[color=#8d1d75]Code Violet[/color]: There is a biohazard threat on board the station.
Any alert code that represents an escalation in station alert level should be accompanied by an announcement explaining the reason for calling the code. This announcement should be done in a timely manner by the individual calling the alert.
## Security
1. Security standard equipment will be specified within their respective alert code and role SOP documents.
2. Codes Yellow and Orange are to be treated as identical to the previous alert code for equipment unless ordered otherwise by the Head of Security or Captain.
3. Any and all available equipment may be used on Codes Gamma and Delta, unless ordered otherwise by the Head of Security, Captain, or Central Command.
4. Security personnel should defer to Central Command for equipment standards on Code Epsilon.
